examples.name: Advanced: AHD Envelopes
examples.description: Demonstrates AHD (Attack-Hold-Decay) envelopes. Compare short staccato vs sustained organ-like tones.

examples.name: Advanced: Ambient Drone
examples.description: Slow, evolving drone with high reverb and long decays for meditative atmosphere.

examples.name: Advanced: Krell Patch
examples.description: A 'Krell' style generative patch with random notes and varying envelope lengths.

examples.name: Advanced: Blues Scale
examples.description: Jamming in blues scale with quantizer and gate for authentic bluesy feel.

examples.name: Advanced: CV Routing
examples.description: Multiple LFOs modulate filter cutoff, pan, and gain for complex modulation effects.

examples.name: Advanced: Delay Network
examples.description: Multiple interconnected delays create a complex echo network with pitch shifting.

examples.name: Demo: Generative Ambient
examples.description: A self-evolving ambient piece with random notes and delays.

examples.name: Demo: Arpeggio
examples.description: A chord broken into individual notes using fixed-timing edges for precise rhythm.

examples.name: Demo: Generative Bells
examples.description: Random bell-like tones with high reverb for an ambient, church-bell atmosphere.

examples.name: Demo: Canon
examples.description: A 2-voice canon: the same melody plays in both voices, with the second voice delayed.

examples.name: Demo: Drum Pattern
examples.description: A basic drum kit using different waveforms and pitches.

examples.name: Demo: Dynamics
examples.description: Demonstrates volume dynamics using gain nodes - loud, soft, and swelling passages.

examples.name: Demo: Filter Bass
examples.description: A bass line with filter modulation for that classic 'wah' sound.

examples.name: Demo: First Song
examples.description: A complete piece combining bass, melody with randomness, and a beat.

examples.name: Demo: Fixed Edge Timing
examples.description: Shows edge timing modes: physical (distance-based) vs fixed (beat-based) travel time.

examples.name: Demo: Fugue
examples.description: A 2-voice fugue: voice 2 enters transposed up a fifth (7 semitones) after a delay.

examples.name: Demo: Simple Melody
examples.description: A 4-note melody created by chaining speakers with pitch shifts.

examples.name: Demo: Mozart's Dice Game
examples.description: An aleatoric system inspired by Musikalisches Würfelspiel. A Splitter creates parallel paths, and Gates randomly allow only some to pass, creating ever-changing melodies.

examples.name: Demo: Polymetric Ambient
examples.description: Three independent loops of 5, 7, and 9 beats phase against each other.

examples.name: Demo: Polyrhythm
examples.description: Three independent rhythms at 4, 3, and 5 beats create shifting patterns.

examples.name: Demo: Sequential Melody
examples.description: A scale pattern using chained speakers with pitch shifts - packets pass through each speaker.

examples.name: Demo: Techno Beat
examples.description: A basic 4-on-the-floor techno pattern with filtered bass and hi-hats.

examples.name: Emergence
examples.description: Three movements grown from one seed, in D dorian. I. Seeds: a rising arpeggio built purely from distance. II. Dialogue: two offset voices breed melodies at a crossover, their offspring rung as bells. III. Chorus: mutation and harmonic selection bloom into a full ensemble under a breathing filter. Play the movements in order from the Scene panel.

examples.name: Advanced: Complex Rhythms
examples.description: Gates with different probabilities create Euclidean-style distributed rhythms.

examples.name: Tutorial: Filter Types
examples.description: Learn the four filter types: Lowpass (removes highs), Highpass (removes lows), Bandpass (isolates a band), and Notch (removes a band). Each scene demonstrates one filter type with the same source for easy comparison.

examples.name: Advanced: Gamelan
examples.description: Indonesian gamelan-inspired metallic tones with interlocking rhythms and harmonics.

examples.name: Advanced: Generative Sequencer
examples.description: Gates and quantizers create an ever-evolving melodic sequence with controlled randomness.

examples.name: Evolutionary: Genetic Melodies
examples.description: Demonstrates genetic algorithm nodes: Mutator adds random variations, Fitness Gate filters out dissonant notes, creating melodies that naturally evolve toward harmony.

examples.name: Advanced: Gravity Tempo
examples.description: Demonstrates gravity physics - heavy nodes (high mass) slow down approaching packets, creating ritardando effects.

examples.name: Advanced: Harmonic Series
examples.description: Oscillators at integer frequency ratios build a rich organ-like tone with natural overtones.

examples.name: Advanced: Layered Pad
examples.description: Uses a tunnel to layer multiple waveforms into a rich, complex pad sound.

examples.name: Advanced: LFO Modulation
examples.description: LFO nodes generate continuous values for CV routing to modulate filter cutoff and pan.

examples.name: Orchestral: Night Symphony
examples.description: A nocturnal orchestral piece with pizzicato strings, harp arpeggios, and ethereal choir pads. Inspired by romantic-era night music.

examples.name: Advanced: Noise Percussion
examples.description: White, pink, and brown noise sources create realistic hi-hats, snares, and rumbles.

examples.name: Tutorial: Noise Types
examples.description: Learn the three noise types: White (equal energy per frequency), Pink (-3dB/octave, natural), and Brown (-6dB/octave, deep rumble). Use noise for percussion, textures, and effects.

examples.name: Advanced: Orchestra
examples.description: Three instrument voices built from layered oscillators, modulators, and filters simulating violin, cello, and flute.

examples.name: Orchestral: Bolero Build
examples.description: Inspired by Ravel's Bolero - a hypnotic repetitive melody that builds with layered orchestration. Start minimal, then unmute voices progressively.

examples.name: Tutorial: Oscillator Modes
examples.description: Learn the three oscillator modes: Additive (layering), Ring (multiplication), and FM (frequency modulation). Each scene demonstrates one mode with the same base frequency for easy comparison.

examples.name: Orchestral: Canon in D
examples.description: Pachelbel's Canon - Ground bass (D-A-B-F#-G-D-G-A) with canon melody entering on staggered string voices. One trigger starts the 8-note sequence that cascades through all voices.

examples.name: Advanced: Pentatonic Jam
examples.description: A complete jam using quantizer for pentatonic scale, LFO modulation, and virtual edges for precise timing.

examples.name: Advanced: Quantizer
examples.description: Random notes snapped to musical scales using quantizers for in-tune generative music.

examples.name: Evolutionary: Radiation Burst
examples.description: Mutator in radiation mode creates dramatic sonic explosions with large pitch jumps and wave changes. Gates control the density of mutations.

examples.name: Advanced: Synth Bass
examples.description: A fat bass sound using multiple waveform layers in a tunnel for synthesis.

examples.name: Advanced: Teleporter
examples.description: Teleporters instantly transport packets to create unique spatial effects and feedback loops.

examples.name: Advanced: Tunnel Melody
examples.description: Demonstrates tunnels creating arpeggios and harmonies with cascading delays.

examples.name: Advanced: Full Tunnel
examples.description: Tunnels containing pitch, oscillator, modulator, and filter for complete synthesis.

examples.name: Tutorial: Learn Stochastic
examples.description: A complete interactive tutorial with 10 scenes teaching you Stochastic from basics to advanced concepts. Use the Scene Panel to navigate between lessons.

examples.name: Tutorial: Unison & Detune
examples.description: Learn how unison voices and detuning create thick, chorus-like sounds. Unison duplicates the oscillator, detune spreads the pitch, and stereo spread places voices across the stereo field.

examples.name: Advanced: Vibrato Strings
examples.description: Modulator nodes add expressive vibrato to create realistic string instrument sounds.

examples.name: Advanced: Virtual Edges
examples.description: Fixed-timing edges for precise rhythmic patterns independent of physical distance.

examples.name: Advanced: Wobble Bass
examples.description: Multiple LFOs at different rates create complex wobble bass movements.
